name: Tamsulosin + Dutasteride
meta: Tamsulosin Hydrochloride: Selective alpha-1A/1D adrenoceptor antagonist; Dutasteride: Dual 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor
Schedule H – prescription only; Dutasteride: Schedule H – prescription only
sections: White crystalline powder (hydrochloride), sparingly soluble in water.
White to pale yellow powder, insoluble in water.

Tamsulosin Hydrochloride: Generic in the USA since 2010; widely used for medical expulsive therapy of distal ureteric stones. First approval/introduction: Japan 1993 (Yamanouchi, now Astellas); US 1997 (Boehringer Ingelheim). Dutasteride: CombAT showed tamsulosin + dutasteride superior to either alone for symptoms and reduced acute urinary retention/surgery; REDUCE found reduced overall prostate cancer detection but more high-grade tumours. First approval/introduction: Patented 1996; US FDA November 2001 (GlaxoSmithKline).
Tamsulosin gives rapid symptom relief by relaxing prostatic smooth muscle; dutasteride shrinks the prostate over months, modifying disease progression (CombAT study).

Tamsulosin Hydrochloride Blocks alpha-1A and alpha-1D receptors in prostatic, bladder-neck and distal ureteric smooth muscle, improving urinary flow in BPH and facilitating passage of distal ureteric stones. Receptor / target profile: Selective antagonist at alpha-1A and alpha-1D receptors in prostate, bladder neck and ureter.

Dutasteride Inhibits both type 1 and type 2 5-alpha-reductase isoenzymes, reducing conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone (~90% DHT reduction), shrinking prostate volume and reducing risk of acute urinary retention and BPH-related surgery. Receptor / target profile: Competitive, irreversible inhibitor of type 1 and type 2 (and 3) 5-alpha-reductase, lowering serum DHT by >90%.
Summary: Modified release; bioavailability ~100% fasting; Tmax 4–5 h (6–7 h fed). ~99% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP3A4 and CYP2D6. Half-life 9–15 h.
